title: Lesson 23: Measuring Outcomes and Reporting Value to the Buyer
description: Proving an agent's value to the buyer by measuring outcomes instead of activity, freezing a baseline before the build, handling the counterfactual, and reporting in the buyer's language on their rhythm.

questions.question: Which kind of number belongs in a report to the buyer?
options: The number of sessions and tokens the agent consumed over the period
The business effect the buyer would have paid for without the agent
The uptime percentage of the agent's runtime environment
The number of successful runs the scheduler completed this month
questions.explanation: Activity metrics describe the machinery and tell the buyer nothing they can act on. A number is worth reporting only when it maps to something the buyer would have paid for anyway.

questions.question: When must the baseline for an outcome metric be captured, and why?
options: At the end of the engagement, drawn from the client's memory of the old process
Whenever it is convenient once the agent is already running in production
Before the solution exists, from the client's real data, agreed in writing
Only if the buyer later requests a formal before-and-after comparison
questions.explanation: A baseline reconstructed after delivery gets idealized in memory, which makes it contested. Freezing it in writing from real data before the solution exists keeps the comparison honest.

questions.question: How should a consultant handle the possibility that another initiative shares credit for an improvement?
options: Name it first and claim only the share the agent can honestly own
Leave it out of the report so the agent's contribution looks larger
Report only a metric for which no other initiative could apply
Wait for the buyer to raise it and then adjust the numbers afterward
questions.explanation: The buyer will think of the other initiative anyway, so naming it first and conceding its weight keeps the claim credible. Claiming only the provable share is what makes the report believed.
